name: Paper
what: Sheets made by beating plant fibre (hemp, mulberry bark, rags) to a pulp, catching it on a screen and drying it. Invented in China by the second century BCE.
why: Paper is cheaper than parchment and tougher than papyrus. Its arrival made bureaucracies, Islamic science and the printing press possible; each place it reached changed the recipe (rags in Samarkand, watermarks in Fabriano, water-powered mills in Europe).
now: About 400 million tonnes of paper and board are made a year.

sources.cite: Bloom, J. M. (2001). Paper Before Print: The History and Impact of Paper in the Islamic World. Yale University Press.
Tsien, T. H. (1985). Paper and Printing. Science and Civilisation in China 5(1). Cambridge University Press.

stops.note: The first paper mill in the Americas worked at Culhuacán near Mexico City around 1580. Long before, the Maya and Aztecs had made their own bark paper, amate, a separate invention.
William Rittenhouse, a papermaker from the Netherlands, built British North America's first paper mill on a creek near Germantown in 1690.
